articles.image_title: AfD und Russland: DRUZHKIVKA, UKRAINE - SEPTEMBER 4: A Ukrainian flag attached to an anti-drone net flies in the wind on September 4, 2026 in Druzhkivka, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. Since last year, Russian forces have been shelling the settlement around the clock. Before February 2022, up to 67,000 people lived there; now, due to constant shelling and the lack of water, electricity, and gas, only about 3,000 civilians remain. Constant attacks by drones and guided aerial bombs make entering Druzhkivka nearly impossible. (Photo by Yan Dobronosov/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images)

articles.image_title: Politikpodcast: Co-leader of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party Alice Weidel (C) and the AfD's top candidate for the regional elections in Saxony-Anhalt, Ulrich Siegmund (C-R) arrive at the party congress of far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) at the Messe Erfurt fairground in Erfurt, eastern Germany on early July 4, 2026. German police are bracing to guard an annual congress of the far-right AfD party this weekend (July 4-5) against tens of thousands of antifascist demonstrators who are determined to shut it down. The standoff in the city of Erfurt, Thuringia state, comes as the opposition Alternative for Germany party is soaring in national opinion polls ahead of all other parties. (Photo by John MACDOUGALL / AFP via Getty Images)
